$comment: The one declaration of what mutation testing covers. scripts/run-mutation.mjs runs a scope by name; tests/architecture/mutation-covers-source.arch.test.ts checks that no source file falls outside both maps and that package.json has a script per scope. Globs, never file lists: a list goes stale the day a file is added, and the score does not drop, because the mutants that would have died were never generated. A scope with a `break` floor can fail a run and is the only kind run per pull request, when its source changed; telemetry and shared are the two gates. Every other scope has no floor: it runs in the weekly schedule and on a manual run, reports its score and never fails on it. A change to stryker.conf.json, vitest.mutation.config.ts or this file runs every scope; a change to pnpm-lock.yaml runs the canary alone, since it can move Stryker or Vitest; any other change runs only the gated scopes whose source it modifies. The floors of the other scopes were removed, not lowered by a measurement: the target keeps a blocking floor only where the cause is identified (telemetry's calculation logic, shared's pure helpers). A floor is raised to the measured score after a run, never lowered without the reason here. shared is the scope once named kernel (shared/domain and the home-dir resolver, 96); the rest of src/shared is shared-infrastructure. A scope's tests are the test paths whose change runs it per change like its source does: a deleted or weakened test lowers the kill rate and only mutation sees it. Static mutants, the ones in a module-level declaration such as a profile, run only while a file loads: each reloads the environment and reruns every test. Every scope but the canary runs with ignoreStatic, so Stryker reports them Ignored, outside the score, and they never rerun the suite; the profile declarations are held by the shared conformance suite and its mutation proof, not by mutants. The tools scope mutates all of src/contexts/tools, in four shards. canary mutates a fixture, not the product: its static mutant stops a module from loading, which Stryker's vitest runner scores as survived on its own; its dynamic mutants check exact selection through nested suites, repeated spaces, and regex characters. It requires 100 and exactly each dynamic mutant's covering test, so a Stryker or Vitest upgrade cannot quietly bypass tests/mutation/unloadable-file-as-failed-test.ts or widen or lose mutation test selection. A scope's mutate is one glob or a list where a leading ! excludes. installation measures 97.5 over its four shards in the pushed head's mutation job, and has no floor.

excluded.src/contexts/update/application/**: Three one-call use cases over ports: each reads a decision or a cache entry from a double and returns it, so a mutant here dies only to the assertion that already pins the call. The branching they dispatch on is the domain scope's, which is mutated.
excluded.src/contexts/update/infrastructure/**: Adapters over the npm registry, the package managers and the cache file. What they translate is held by the contract suites against a local server and stub binaries; mutating them reruns those servers and subprocesses for every mutant, and the exact strings are pinned by the adapter tests.
excluded.src/contexts/update/ports/**: Interfaces and types only: they compile to nothing, so no mutant can be generated that a test could see.
excluded.src/contexts/host-registration/ports/**: Interfaces and types only: they compile to nothing, so no mutant can be generated that a test could see.
excluded.src/contexts/host-registration/contract/: Types only: they compile to nothing, so no mutant can be generated that a test could see.
excluded.src/contexts/recipes/infrastructure/**: One adapter over the disk. What it translates, the error codes and the directory listing, is held by the contract suite run against it and against the in-memory fake, and its descriptor handling by its integration test; mutating it reruns real temp directories for every mutant.
excluded.src/contexts/recipes/ports/**: Interfaces and types only: they compile to nothing, so no mutant can be generated that a test could see.
excluded.src/cli.ts: The entry point. It registers commands and returns: no branch a mutant could change that a unit or integration test would see, and what proves it runs is the e2e suite, which mutation excludes because it spawns a built binary no mutant reaches.
excluded.src/composition/**/*.ts: Composition modules construct adapters and hand them to commands, with no rule of their own. What drives them is the in-process command tests and the e2e suite, which the mutation run leaves out (vitest.mutation.config.ts), so every mutant there would survive for a reason that says nothing about the tests.
excluded.src/orchestration/**/*.ts: Scenarios sequencing the contexts, with no rule of their own. The e2e suite and the command tests drive them end to end; a mutant there survives or dies on a journey, not on an assertion about one behaviour.
excluded.src/presentation/**/*.ts: Rendering and prompting, with no business logic. The command tests and the e2e suite pin the output; the telemetry display files are mutated by the telemetry scope.
excluded.src/contexts/telemetry/infrastructure/st: Private file permissions on the real disk: a mutant reruns the permission checks on temporary directories, and the modes are pinned by the integration test.
